# QueroCura: full text of the public pages

> QueroCura is an Indian healthcare software platform with two connected parts: a free health app for people and families (symptom checker in English and Hindi, medicine reminders, personal health records called CuraVault, family health management, visit preparation) and a hospital management system (HMS) for clinics and hospitals of any size (appointments with real wait times, OPD tokens, emergency triage, beds, operation theatres, pharmacy, billing with UPI, PM-JAY and CGHS, roles, audit logs and AI-assisted imaging). Patients decide what their hospital can see. QueroCura never recommends medicines and is not a diagnosis.


---

# A hospital management system that runs every hour of your hospital

Source: https://querocura.com/hospital-management-system/

QueroCura is a hospital management system (HMS) for clinics, nursing homes and multi-specialty hospitals in India. It brings the patient register, appointments, OPD queue, emergency triage, beds, operation theatres, pharmacy, billing and reports into one system, and connects to the patient's own health app with their consent.

## What a hospital management system should do, and what QueroCura does

A good HMS removes retyping, waiting and guesswork. Every department should work from the same patient record, the front desk should know when each doctor will really be free, and the accounts team should see what is billed and what is still owed without chasing paper.


| Area | In QueroCura |
|---|---|
| Patient register | One record and MRN per patient: visits, prescriptions, results, scans and bills |
| Appointments | Every doctor's day side by side; each free slot shows when the patient will really be seen |
| OPD queue | Fair tokens by department and a waiting-room screen that never shows names |
| Emergency | Five-level triage with time-to-be-seen targets and early-warning scores |
| In-patients | Live bed board, admission to the right bed, shift handover, discharge checklists and signed summaries |
| Operation theatres | Theatre lists with clash checks and the WHO surgical safety checklist in every case |
| Pharmacy | Allergy and duplicate checks, printable prescriptions, stock dispensed by expiry |
| Billing | Bills fill themselves from the visit; cash, UPI and card with receipts; PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance payers |
| Imaging | AI-assisted draft reads that a radiologist accepts, rejects and signs; an on-premise option keeps images on your server |
| Reports | Footfall, admissions, collections and occupancy, live and as CSV, in a command centre |

## Appointments that follow the real day

A 10:00 appointment means little if the doctor is twenty minutes behind. QueroCura watches each doctor's day as it happens: who is with them, who is waiting and how long their consultations usually take. It predicts when each patient will really be seen, highlights the slot with the shortest real wait, and tells patients when to arrive. Patients using the QueroCura app are told on the day if their doctor is running late.


## Sized to your hospital, from a single clinic to many branches

- **A setup plan in about two minutes.** Answer questions about beds, doctors and services; one click creates your departments, wards, beds, theatres and price list.
- **Several sites.** Branches with their own departments, wards, queue, bed board and front-desk board, with staff assigned to the sites they work at.
- **Roles you design.** Change what each role can do, or create your own, such as "Senior receptionist". Front desk and billing never see clinical notes.
- **Run it alongside what you have.** For many clinics and nursing homes QueroCura can be the day-to-day system; larger hospitals can run it next to an existing HIS for patient-consented records.

## Built for Indian hospitals

- Payments by cash, UPI and card; PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance payers.
- ABHA ready, with your ABDM facility ID on your organisation profile.
- English and Hindi for patients, end to end.
- Every organisation is verified with its registration or licence number before it can reach a patient.

## Security and patient consent

Staff sign in with a password and an authenticator code, and idle sessions end on their own. Every request, view and change goes into a hash-chained audit log that nobody can edit, and patients can see their own part of it. Clinical text is encrypted at rest. A hospital sees a patient's app data only if the patient connects and chooses what to share, with an end date and an off switch.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a hospital management system?**

A hospital management system (HMS) is software that runs a hospital's daily work in one place: patient registration, appointments and queues, emergency and in-patient care, theatres, pharmacy, billing and reports. QueroCura is an HMS built for hospitals and clinics in India.

**Which is the best hospital management system for a small hospital or clinic in India?**

The right HMS is the one your team will actually use: quick to set up, priced for your size, with UPI billing, PM-JAY and CGHS support, ABHA readiness and role-based access. QueroCura creates a setup plan sized to your facility in about two minutes and can be the day-to-day system for clinics and nursing homes. Our buyer's guide lists what to check before choosing any HMS.

**Does QueroCura support PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance?**

Yes. Bills can be raised to PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance payers, alongside cash, UPI and card payments with receipts.

**Is QueroCura ABHA and ABDM ready?**

Yes. Organisations can record their ABDM facility ID, and patients can keep their ABHA on their QueroCura profile.

**Can QueroCura handle more than one branch?**

Yes. Sites have their own departments, wards, queue and bed board, and staff are assigned to the sites they work at.

**How much does the QueroCura hospital management system cost?**

We are onboarding our first hospitals now and price by size. Plan your setup online or write to hello@querocura.com and we will talk.

# Clinic management software for doctors who would rather see patients than paperwork

Source: https://querocura.com/clinic-management-software/

QueroCura gives a doctor practising alone, or a clinic with a few doctors, one place for opening hours and bookings, today's patients, prescriptions, bills and practice insights. Patients who use the QueroCura app can arrive with their history, readings and questions already shared with you.

## Everything a clinic runs on

- **Hours and bookings.** Set your hours; patients book real free slots, and each slot shows when they are likely to be seen.
- **Today's patients.** A list of who is booked, who has arrived and who is with you.
- **OPD tokens.** A fair token queue and a waiting-room screen that shows token numbers, never names.
- **Prescriptions.** Printable prescriptions with allergy and duplicate checks.
- **Billing.** Bills fill from the visit; collect by cash, UPI or card with receipts; set prices per doctor and per test.
- **Practice insights.** Footfall, collections and how your days actually run.

## Patients who arrive prepared

Patients using QueroCura can send you a one-page brief before the visit: why they are coming, what worries them most and what has changed in their readings, behind a link that needs a PIN and expires on its own. You see what they chose to share, and nothing else.


## Grow from one doctor to a hospital without changing systems

The same software runs a hospital: add departments, wards and beds, emergency triage, theatres and pharmacy when you need them, and invite your team with the role that fits each person.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is clinic management software?**

Clinic management software runs a clinic's day: appointments, the waiting queue, patient records, prescriptions and billing. QueroCura does this for single doctors and multi-doctor clinics in India.

**Is there clinic software with UPI billing?**

Yes. QueroCura collects by cash, UPI or card and gives receipts, with prices set per doctor and per test.

**Can patients book appointments online?**

Yes. Patients book real free slots, see when they are likely to be seen, and get told on the day if the doctor is running late.

**Can I start as a single doctor and add a clinic later?**

Yes. Start on your own; when you open or join a clinic, the same account works inside it.

# Doctor appointment booking that shows when patients will really be seen

Source: https://querocura.com/doctor-appointment-booking/

Most booking systems hand out fixed slots that drift as the day runs late. QueroCura predicts the real start time of every slot from each doctor's own recent consultations, points the front desk and the patient to the shortest real wait, and keeps the waiting room quiet.

## How it works

- **Live status of every doctor:** free now, with a patient, or running late, at a glance on the front-desk board.
- **The best slot, highlighted:** every free slot shows when the patient will really be seen, and the soonest real start is marked.
- **Arrive-by times:** the desk tells patients when to come, and the app warns them on the day if their doctor is running late.
- **Learns each doctor:** predictions use each doctor's own consultations, not a fixed slot length.

## OPD tokens and the waiting room

Tokens are issued fairly by department. The waiting-room screen shows token numbers and room names only, never a patient's name, and each screen has its own private link that an administrator can switch off at any time.


## For patients

Book a visit with a doctor or clinic on QueroCura, see the time you are likely to be seen, add it to your calendar and get reminders. Visit prep helps you write down why you are going and what to ask.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is an OPD queue management system?**

It issues tokens to out-patients, calls them in order and shows the queue on a waiting-room screen. QueroCura's queue issues fair tokens by department and never shows names on the screen.

**Can patients see the doctor's real waiting time?**

Yes. Each free slot shows when the patient will really be seen, based on how the doctor's day is actually running.


---

# AI-assisted imaging reads that your radiologist stays in charge of

Source: https://querocura.com/ai-medical-imaging/

QueroCura's imaging workspace views X-ray, CT and MRI series, ultrasound, ECG and more, and can prepare an AI draft read for a qualified clinician to review. The QueroCura Vision Engine can run on the hospital's own server, so images never leave it. It is decision support, not a diagnosis: every finding is accepted or rejected and the report signed by your clinician.

## What the on-premise engine reads


| Study | What it does |
|---|---|
| Chest X-ray (frontal, adult) | Two independently trained models read for 18 findings, behind safety checks that refuse lateral views, other body parts and unusual images. Heatmap boxes show where the model looked. |
| 12-lead ECG (digital waveform) | Signal quality per lead, rhythm (including atrial fibrillation and broad-complex tachycardia), PR, QRS, QT and QTc, axis, bundle-branch blocks, and ST elevation by published criteria. |
| CT chest and head (DICOM series) | Hounsfield-unit measurements: lung nodule candidates with Fleischner follow-up, an emphysema index, and possible acute intracranial blood with midline shift. |

## Built to avoid confident mistakes

- Each reader refuses rather than guesses when an image or trace is outside what it was built for, and says why.
- Can't-miss chest findings such as pneumothorax are shown as "possible" when either model flags them.
- Every model is pinned and checksummed; nothing runs from an altered file.
- Hospitals validate the models on their own labelled cases; until then every draft says it is not yet validated there.
- Clinicians' accept and reject decisions are tallied per model, with a warning if a model's findings are mostly rejected.

## The radiologist decides

Patients never see an unsigned draft. AI is off until an administrator switches it on, and patients can opt out of AI help with their own scans. QueroCura's imaging AI is not a cleared medical device and can be wrong or miss things.


## Frequently asked questions

**Does QueroCura's AI diagnose scans?**

No. It prepares a draft for a qualified clinician, who accepts or rejects every finding and signs the report. It is decision support, not a diagnosis or a cleared medical device.

**Can AI imaging run without sending images to the cloud?**

Yes. The QueroCura Vision Engine can run on the hospital's own server on ordinary CPUs, so images never leave the hospital.

**Which scans can it read?**

On-premise: frontal adult chest X-rays, digital 12-lead ECGs and CT chest or head series. Other studies are viewed and reported by your clinicians as usual.

# A medicine reminder app that keeps the whole family in the loop

Source: https://querocura.com/medicine-reminder-app/

QueroCura reminds you to take each dose at the times on the prescriptions you confirmed. Tap Taken right on the notification, and the family members you allow are told straight away, so a parent's or child's medicines never depend on memory alone. It is free, and it works in English and Hindi.

## How the reminders work

- **Timed to your prescriptions.** Add a prescription (or let CuraVault read it from a photo) and confirm the doses; reminders follow those times.
- **Taken, from the notification.** Mark a dose as taken without opening the app.
- **Family alerts.** People you give permission to are notified when a dose is taken, for example "Aarav (your child) has taken his morning dose".
- **On your phone or computer.** Notifications arrive through your browser, with no app store needed.
- **Your visits too.** The health calendar reminds you of appointments and tests, and exports to any calendar.

## Reminders, never recommendations

QueroCura reminds you to take what your doctor prescribed. It never suggests a medicine, a dose or a change: those decisions stay with your doctor.


## Looking after someone else's medicines

Caring for an elderly parent? Connect your QueroCura accounts in the family garden and choose what you can see. With permission for Medicines, you can follow their doses and be told when they are taken, from anywhere.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is the best free medicine reminder app in India?**

Look for reminders timed to your actual prescriptions, an easy way to mark a dose taken, family alerts for people you care for, and Hindi support. QueroCura does all of these and is free.

**Can I get reminders for my parents' medicines?**

Yes. Connect your accounts in QueroCura's family garden with permission for Medicines, and you are told when their doses are taken.

**Does the app tell me which medicine to take?**

No. QueroCura only reminds you about medicines your doctor prescribed and you confirmed. It never recommends a medicine or dose.

**Does it work in Hindi?**

Yes. The whole app, including reminders, works in English and Hindi.

# Manage your family's health together, with everyone's permission

Source: https://querocura.com/family-health-app/

QueroCura's family garden connects the QueroCura accounts of the people you care for, so you can look after parents, children and partners from one place. Each person decides exactly what you can see and do: medicines, records, vitals, symptom checks, or editing their profile. Updates arrive instantly, such as when a parent takes their medicine.

## Permissions, one area at a time


| Permission | What it lets you do |
|---|---|
| Medicines | See their medicines and doses, and be told when a dose is taken |
| Records | See the reports and prescriptions in their CuraVault |
| Vitals | Follow readings such as blood pressure, glucose and weight over time |
| Symptom checks | See the symptom checks they have done and how urgent they were |
| Edit profile | Help keep their profile, allergies and details up to date |

## Real accounts, real consent

Everyone in the family garden has their own QueroCura account, so nobody's health information is held by someone else without their knowledge. A connection is made with an invitation, each person chooses the areas they share, and either side can change or end it at any time.


## Everything the family needs

- Symptom checks in English and Hindi that say how urgent things look and when to see a doctor.
- CuraVault for each person's reports, prescriptions and scans.
- Medicine reminders with a Taken button and family alerts.
- A health calendar for visits, tests and follow-ups.
- Visit prep and a one-page doctor brief before an appointment.

## Frequently asked questions

**How can I manage my family's health in one app?**

In QueroCura, connect your family members' accounts in the family garden and choose permissions for each area (medicines, records, vitals, symptom checks, profile). You then see what each person shares with you, in one place.

**Can I track my elderly parents' health from another city?**

Yes. With their permission you can follow their medicines and readings and are notified when they take a dose.

**Can I add my child?**

Each family member connects with their own QueroCura account, and you choose together what you can see and do.

**Is the family health app free?**

Yes. Signing up and using QueroCura's personal and family features is free.

# Your medical reports, in one place, explained in plain language

Source: https://querocura.com/personal-health-records/

CuraVault is QueroCura's personal health record. Upload a blood test, scan report or prescription, even a handwritten one; it reads the values, lets you check them, explains each one in plain language and tracks them over time. Your records are encrypted, and you decide who sees them.

## What CuraVault does

- **Reads your reports.** Lab reports, scan reports and prescriptions, including handwritten ones. You confirm what was read.
- **Explains each value.** What a result like HbA1c or vitamin D means, in plain language, and how it compares with your earlier results.
- **Notices change.** Insights flag a creeping blood pressure, a sudden weight drop or a result that keeps coming back.
- **Brings your readings in.** Import blood pressure, glucose, SpO2, weight, steps and sleep from Apple Health, Google Fit or a spreadsheet; the file is read on your device.
- **Shares on your terms.** Share links need a PIN, expire, have a view limit and can be turned off in one tap; a hospital sees nothing until you say yes.

## Private by design

Records are encrypted. Every look by anyone other than you is written to an access log you can read. You can download everything QueroCura holds about you in one file, and delete your account and all of it yourself, whenever you choose.


## Works alongside ABHA

ABHA is India's digital health ID for linking records across participating providers. CuraVault is your own record of your health story: readings, symptom history, medicines and reports. They complement each other.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a personal health record app?**

A personal health record (PHR) app keeps your own medical reports, prescriptions and readings in one place that you control. QueroCura's CuraVault also reads your reports and explains them.

**Can an app read my lab report and explain it?**

Yes. Upload a lab report to CuraVault, check the values it read, and it explains each one in plain language and tracks it over time. It does not diagnose or recommend medicines.

**Is my health data safe?**

Records are encrypted, shared only when you choose, and every access by someone else is logged for you to see. You can export or delete everything at any time.

# A symptom checker that asks the questions a doctor would

Source: https://querocura.com/symptom-checker/

Type or speak how you feel, in English or Hindi. QueroCura's symptom checker asks a few follow-up questions, each chosen to rule something in or out, then tells you how urgent things look, what is safe at home, what to avoid and when to see a doctor. It takes about two minutes, is free, and never tells you which medicine to take.

## How a check works

- **Say it your way.** No medical words needed, in English or Hindi.
- **Cura asks what matters.** A clinical-interview style: the next most useful question, with the reason it asks.
- **Know what to do next.** A clear urgency level, what is safe at home, and the warning signs that mean you should go now.

## What it knows

The symptom engine covers 55 health conditions and more than 130 symptoms and warning signs, with seasonal patterns that matter in India, such as dengue and malaria in the monsoon. It only shows a result once it is confident enough.


## What it is not

A symptom check shows patterns that fit what you described and how urgent things look. It is a starting point for a conversation with your doctor, not a diagnosis, and it never recommends a medicine. In an emergency, call 112.


## Frequently asked questions

**Is there a symptom checker in Hindi?**

Yes. QueroCura's symptom checker works end to end in Hindi: you can describe symptoms in Hindi and get the questions and results in Hindi.

**Is an online symptom checker accurate?**

No symptom checker can replace a doctor. QueroCura asks follow-up questions like a clinical interview, shows a result only when confident enough, and is clear about urgency and when to see a doctor.

**Does it recommend medicines?**

No. QueroCura never tells you which medicine to take.

# How to choose a hospital management system: a practical checklist

Source: https://querocura.com/guides/how-to-choose-a-hospital-management-system/

Searching for the top hospital management systems gives you long lists and little help choosing. The best HMS for your hospital is the one that fits your size, your payers and your team. Use this checklist to compare any system, including ours.

## 1. Start with your own problems

Write down the three things that hurt most today: a crowded waiting room, lost revenue at billing, beds you can't see, or records that don't follow the patient. Judge every system by how it fixes those, not by the length of its module list.


## 2. The modules a hospital actually uses


| Module | Ask the vendor |
|---|---|
| Registration & records | Is there one record per patient across departments and visits? |
| Appointments & OPD | Does booking reflect how late doctors are really running? Is the token screen private? |
| Emergency | Is there structured triage with time targets? |
| In-patients | Is the bed board live? Are handover and discharge checklists built in? |
| Theatres | Are clashes caught? Is the WHO surgical safety checklist built in? |
| Pharmacy | Are allergies and duplicates checked? Is stock dispensed by expiry? |
| Billing | UPI, PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance? Do bills fill from the visit? |
| Reports | Live occupancy, footfall and collections, exportable? |

## 3. India-specific must-haves

- UPI and card collection with receipts.
- PM-JAY, CGHS and insurance payers.
- ABHA and ABDM readiness.
- Patient-facing language support (at least English and Hindi).

## 4. Security and consent

- Two-step sign-in for staff.
- Role-based access where front desk and billing can't read clinical notes.
- A tamper-evident audit log.
- Encryption at rest, and a clear answer to who owns the data.
- Patient consent for anything shared from outside the hospital.

## 5. Setup time, size and cost

Ask how long it takes from signing to the first patient, whether the vendor can create your departments, wards, beds and price list for you, and how pricing changes as you add doctors, beds or branches. A system that takes months to configure costs more than its licence.


## 6. Try it on a real day

Run a pilot with your front desk, one doctor and your billing desk for a week. Count waiting time, billing gaps and retyping before and after. That tells you more than any demo.


## Frequently asked questions

**What are the most important features of a hospital management system?**

One patient record across departments, appointments and OPD queues, emergency triage, a live bed board, pharmacy checks, billing with UPI and government schemes, role-based access, an audit log and live reports.

**How long does it take to set up an HMS?**

It ranges from days to months. QueroCura produces a setup plan in about two minutes and creates departments, wards, beds, theatres and a price list in one click.

# BMI calculator with Indian cut-offs

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/bmi-calculator/

Body mass index (BMI) is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. Indians develop diabetes and heart disease at lower BMIs than Europeans, so Indian guidelines use lower cut-offs: overweight from 23 and obese from 25. This calculator shows both.

## BMI categories


| Category | Asian-Indian cut-off | WHO international |
|---|---|---|
| Underweight | Below 18.5 | Below 18.5 |
| Normal | 18.5 to 22.9 | 18.5 to 24.9 |
| Overweight | 23 to 24.9 | 25 to 29.9 |
| Obese | 25 or more | 30 or more |

## How it's calculated

BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². The Asian-Indian cut-offs come from the 2009 Indian consensus guidelines on obesity, which lowered them because of higher body fat and metabolic risk at the same BMI.

BMI does not measure body fat directly: very muscular people can score high, and older people can score normal while carrying too much fat. Waist size adds useful information (risk rises above 90 cm for Indian men and 80 cm for Indian women).


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a normal BMI for Indians?**

18.5 to 22.9. Indian guidelines treat 23 to 24.9 as overweight and 25 or more as obese, lower than the WHO international cut-offs.

**Is BMI accurate?**

It is a quick screening number, not a diagnosis. It does not tell muscle from fat; waist size and a doctor's assessment add to it.


---

# Is my blood pressure normal? Check a reading

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/blood-pressure-checker/

Enter the top (systolic) and bottom (diastolic) numbers of a reading. The checker shows which category it falls in under the International Society of Hypertension 2020 guideline. One reading is not a diagnosis: blood pressure is judged on several readings taken on different days.

## Blood pressure categories (ISH 2020, adults, clinic readings)


| Category | Systolic (top) | Diastolic (bottom) |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | Below 130 | and below 85 |
| High-normal | 130 to 139 | or 85 to 89 |
| Grade 1 hypertension | 140 to 159 | or 90 to 99 |
| Grade 2 hypertension | 160 or more | or 100 or more |

## When it is urgent

A reading of 180/110 or higher needs medical attention the same day. Go to an emergency department now if a high reading comes with chest pain, breathlessness, a severe headache, confusion, weakness on one side, blurred vision or trouble speaking. In India, call 112.


## Measuring it right

- Sit quietly for five minutes, back supported, feet flat, arm resting at heart level.
- No caffeine, smoking or exercise in the 30 minutes before.
- Take two readings a minute apart and use the average.
- Home readings run lower than clinic ones: 135/85 at home is roughly equivalent to 140/90 in a clinic.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is normal blood pressure?**

Under the ISH 2020 guideline, below 130/85 is normal for adults. Hypertension starts at 140/90 on repeated clinic readings.

**Is 140/90 high blood pressure?**

Yes, 140/90 or above on repeated readings is grade 1 hypertension. Talk to your doctor; do not start or change medicines on your own.


---

# HbA1c to average blood sugar

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/hba1c-to-average-glucose/

HbA1c shows your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. Enter an HbA1c percentage to see the estimated average glucose (eAG) it corresponds to, or enter an average glucose to see the matching HbA1c.

## HbA1c ranges


| HbA1c | Meaning (ADA) | Average glucose |
|---|---|---|
| Below 5.7% | Normal | below about 117 mg/dL |
| 5.7% to 6.4% | Prediabetes | about 117 to 137 mg/dL |
| 6.5% or more | Diabetes range (confirm with a repeat test) | about 140 mg/dL or more |

## How it's calculated

The ADAG study formula: average glucose (mg/dL) = 28.7 × HbA1c − 46.7, or in mmol/L = 1.59 × HbA1c − 2.59. Anaemia, recent blood loss or transfusion, pregnancy, kidney disease and some haemoglobin variants can make HbA1c misleading; your doctor reads it with those in mind.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a normal HbA1c?**

Below 5.7%. 5.7% to 6.4% is prediabetes and 6.5% or more is in the diabetes range.

**HbA1c 7 means what blood sugar?**

An HbA1c of 7% corresponds to an estimated average glucose of about 154 mg/dL (8.6 mmol/L).


---

# Pregnancy due date calculator

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/pregnancy-due-date/

Enter the first day of your last menstrual period and your usual cycle length. The calculator gives your estimated due date, how far along you are today and your trimester. An early ultrasound scan gives a more exact date.

## How it's calculated

Naegele's rule: the due date is 280 days (40 weeks) after the first day of the last period, adjusted by the difference between your cycle length and 28 days. Only about 1 in 20 babies arrives on the due date; most arrive within two weeks either side.


## Trimesters


| Trimester | Weeks |
|---|---|
| First | Up to 13 weeks 6 days |
| Second | 14 to 27 weeks 6 days |
| Third | 28 weeks to birth |

## Frequently asked questions

**How accurate is a due date calculator?**

It is an estimate. A dating ultrasound in the first trimester is more accurate, especially with irregular cycles.

# Make a printable medicine schedule

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/medicine-schedule-maker/

Write down each medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed it, tick the times of day, and print a clear chart to stick on the fridge. Everything stays in your browser. For reminders on your phone with a Taken button and family alerts, use the QueroCura app.

## Tips for a medicine chart that works

- Copy names and doses exactly from the prescription; ask your pharmacist if anything is unclear.
- Note "before food" or "after food" where the prescription says so.
- Keep the chart next to the medicines, and a photo of it on your phone.
- Bring the chart and the medicines to every doctor's visit.

## Frequently asked questions

**Does this tell me what medicines to take?**

No. Fill it in from your doctor's prescription. QueroCura never recommends medicines or doses.

# QTc calculator (four formulas)

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/qtc-calculator/

Enter the measured QT interval and the heart rate. The calculator gives the corrected QT by Bazett, Fridericia, Framingham and Hodges. Fridericia is preferred at fast or slow rates, where Bazett over- and under-corrects.

## Formulas


| Formula | QTc = |
|---|---|
| Bazett | QT ÷ √RR |
| Fridericia | QT ÷ ∛RR |
| Framingham | QT + 154 × (1 − RR) |
| Hodges | QT + 1.75 × (HR − 60) |

## Thresholds

Prolonged: over 450 ms in men, over 470 ms in women. 500 ms or more, or a rise of 60 ms or more from baseline, carries a high risk of torsades de pointes. RR is in seconds (60 ÷ heart rate). With a QRS of 120 ms or more, the JT interval is a better guide.


## Frequently asked questions

**Which QTc formula is best?**

Fridericia and Framingham correct better than Bazett at heart rates outside 60 to 100; Bazett remains common but overestimates QTc at fast rates.


---

# Bed occupancy rate and length-of-stay calculator

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/bed-occupancy-rate/

Four numbers hospital managers watch every month. Enter your bed count, the period, inpatient days and discharges to get bed occupancy rate, average length of stay (ALOS), bed turnover rate and turnover interval.

## Formulas


| Indicator | Formula |
|---|---|
| Bed occupancy rate | Inpatient days ÷ (beds × days in period) × 100 |
| Average length of stay | Inpatient days ÷ discharges |
| Bed turnover rate | Discharges ÷ beds |
| Turnover interval | (Beds × days − inpatient days) ÷ discharges |

## What good looks like

Many hospitals aim for 75% to 85% occupancy: lower wastes capacity, while running above about 85% leaves little room for emergencies and is linked to bed shortages and infection risk. ALOS depends heavily on case mix, so compare it within a specialty and over time.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a good bed occupancy rate?**

Around 75% to 85% is a common target. Sustained occupancy above 85% leaves too little room for emergency admissions.

**How do you calculate average length of stay?**

Total inpatient days in a period divided by the number of discharges in the same period.

# OPD capacity and waiting time calculator

Source: https://querocura.com/calculators/opd-capacity-planner/

Enter how many doctors are in OPD, their hours and the average consultation time. The planner shows how many patients you can see per day and per hour, and how long a patient arriving now will wait behind those already in the queue.

## How it's calculated

Capacity per day = doctors × hours × 60 ÷ consultation minutes. Expected wait for a new arrival ≈ patients waiting × consultation minutes ÷ doctors. Real days drift: consultations vary and doctors start late. QueroCura learns each doctor's real consultation times and shows the real wait for every slot.


## Frequently asked questions

**How do you reduce OPD waiting time?**

Book patients for when the doctor will really be free, spread arrivals with arrive-by times, separate quick follow-ups, and show the queue honestly. See our guide on reducing OPD waiting time.


---

# How to reduce OPD waiting time: 8 practical fixes

Source: https://querocura.com/guides/how-to-reduce-opd-waiting-time/

Most OPD waiting comes from one mismatch: patients are booked for the time on the schedule, but doctors run to the time of the real day. Fixing that mismatch, and being honest with patients about it, does more than adding chairs to the waiting room.

## 1. Measure the real wait first

Record arrival time, time called and time seen for a week. Most clinics find the wait is concentrated in two or three peak hours and with one or two doctors, which tells you where to act.


## 2. Book to the real consultation length

Fixed 10-minute slots fail when a doctor really averages 14. Book each doctor to their own average consultation time, and recalculate it every few weeks.


## 3. Give arrive-by times, not slot times

Tell patients when to arrive based on when the doctor will really be free, and warn them on the day if the doctor is running late. Fewer people arrive early and sit for an hour.


## 4. Separate quick visits

Report reviews, dressing changes and prescription renewals take minutes. A separate queue or time block for them stops them waiting behind new consultations.


## 5. Do the paperwork before the patient reaches the doctor

Registration, vitals and history-taking at the front desk or by a nurse, and patients who send their history before the visit, save minutes in every consultation.


## 6. Use fair, visible tokens

A token per department and a waiting-room screen that shows the queue (by number, never by name) reduces anxiety and the stream of "how much longer?" questions at the desk.


## 7. Watch every doctor's status live

The desk should see at a glance who is free, who is with a patient and who is running late, and send walk-ins to the doctor with the shortest real wait.


## 8. Review weekly

Look at waiting times by doctor and hour every week and adjust slots and staffing. Small changes compound.


## Frequently asked questions

**What is a reasonable OPD waiting time?**

Many hospitals aim for patients to be seen within 30 minutes of their appointment time; publish your own target and measure against it.


---

# How to help elderly parents take their medicines on time

Source: https://querocura.com/guides/how-to-remind-elderly-parents-to-take-medicines/

Missed and doubled doses are common when parents take several medicines a day, and harder to spot when you live in another city. A clear list, a simple routine and reminders that tell you when a dose has been taken make the biggest difference.

## 1. Make one up-to-date list

Gather every prescription and every strip in the house. Write one list with each medicine, its dose, when to take it and what it is for, and ask their doctor or pharmacist to check it, especially if several doctors prescribe. Our free medicine schedule maker prints one.


## 2. Tie doses to daily habits

Morning tea, lunch and the evening news are easier to remember than clock times. Keep the medicines where that habit happens, away from heat and children.


## 3. Use a weekly pill organiser

A box with morning, afternoon and night compartments for each day shows at a glance whether a dose was taken. Fill it together once a week, or ask a neighbour or pharmacist to help.


## 4. Set reminders that close the loop

A reminder only helps if someone knows the dose was taken. With QueroCura, your parent taps Taken on the reminder and, with their permission, you are told straight away. If no confirmation comes, you know to call.


## 5. Watch for side effects and changes

Dizziness, falls, confusion or new sleepiness after a medicine change are worth a call to the doctor. Never stop or change a medicine without the doctor's advice.


## 6. Take the list to every visit

Bring the list and the medicines themselves to each appointment so the doctor can review everything together, and update the list the same day.


## Frequently asked questions

**How can I check if my parents took their medicine when I live far away?**

Use a reminder app with family alerts. In QueroCura, your parent marks a dose as taken and, with their permission, you are notified immediately.


---

# EMR vs EHR vs HMS vs PHR: what's the difference?

Source: https://querocura.com/guides/emr-vs-ehr-vs-hms/

These four terms are often used as if they mean the same thing. In short: an EMR is one provider's clinical record, an EHR is a record designed to follow the patient between providers, an HMS runs the hospital's operations, and a PHR belongs to the patient.

## At a glance


|  | Who owns it | What it holds | Example use |
|---|---|---|---|
| EMR (electronic medical record) | One clinic or hospital | Diagnoses, notes, prescriptions, results at that provider | A doctor reviewing last month's visit |
| EHR (electronic health record) | Shared across providers | A patient's record from many providers, built to be exchanged | A specialist seeing a GP's history |
| HMS / HIS (hospital management or information system) | The hospital | Operations: registration, appointments, beds, theatres, pharmacy, billing, plus the EMR | Running the OPD queue and billing |
| PHR (personal health record) | The patient | Reports, prescriptions, readings and history the patient keeps | A family keeping parents' reports in one place |

## How they fit together in India

ABDM (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission) links these pieces: patients get an ABHA number, facilities register in the Health Facility Registry, and records can move between providers with the patient's consent. A hospital's HMS holds its EMR; the patient's PHR app can receive copies; consent decides who sees what.


## Where QueroCura fits

QueroCura has both ends: a hospital management system with a clinical record for providers, and CuraVault, a personal health record for patients and families, connected by the patient's consent.


## Frequently asked questions

**Is an HMS the same as an EMR?**

No. An HMS runs hospital operations (appointments, beds, pharmacy, billing) and usually contains an EMR, which is the clinical record.

**What is a PHR?**

A personal health record: the patient's own collection of reports, prescriptions and readings, which the patient controls.


---

# How to organise your family's medical records

Source: https://querocura.com/guides/how-to-organise-your-familys-medical-records/

Reports in WhatsApp chats, prescriptions in drawers, scans on CDs: most families' records are scattered until the day a doctor needs them. An hour of organising, then a habit of adding each new report the day it arrives, fixes it.

## 1. One place per person

Give each family member their own folder or record. Mixing everyone's papers is how a parent's report ends up in a child's file.


## 2. Keep these first

- Allergies, long-term conditions and current medicines (one page per person).
- Blood group, ABHA number and insurance details.
- The last two years of lab reports, discharge summaries and scan reports.
- Vaccination records for children and older adults.

## 3. Digitise and name files clearly

Photograph or scan each paper and name it with the date, the person and the test, such as "2026-03-14 Papa HbA1c". In CuraVault, upload the photo: it reads the values, you check them, and each one is explained and tracked over time.


## 4. Share safely

Share only what a doctor needs, for as long as they need it. QueroCura share links need a PIN, expire on their own and can be switched off; a hospital sees nothing until you say yes.


## 5. Make it a habit

Add every new report the day you receive it, and review each person's one-page summary before a visit.


## Frequently asked questions

**Which medical records should I keep?**

Allergies, conditions and current medicines; blood group and insurance; recent lab, scan and discharge reports; and vaccination records.

# Healthcare and hospital glossary

Source: https://querocura.com/glossary/

- **ABDM**: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission: India's national programme to connect patients, health facilities and professionals digitally, with records shared by consent.
- **ABHA**: Ayushman Bharat Health Account: a free 14-digit health ID that lets a person link and share their health records across ABDM-connected providers with consent.
- **ALOS (average length of stay)**: Total inpatient days in a period divided by the number of discharges in that period.
- **Bed occupancy rate**: Inpatient days divided by available bed-days in a period, as a percentage; many hospitals aim for 75% to 85%.
- **CGHS**: Central Government Health Scheme: health cover for central government employees, pensioners and their dependants, used at empanelled hospitals.
- **DICOM**: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine: the standard format for medical images such as X-ray, CT and MRI, and for exchanging them.
- **Discharge summary**: A document given when a patient leaves hospital: diagnosis, treatment given, medicines and follow-up instructions.
- **Early warning score (NEWS2)**: A score from vital signs (breathing rate, oxygen, blood pressure, pulse, consciousness, temperature) that flags patients who are getting worse.
- **EHR (electronic health record)**: A patient's record designed to be shared across providers.
- **EMR (electronic medical record)**: The clinical record kept by one provider.
- **e-Prescription**: A prescription created digitally, which can be checked for allergies and duplicates and printed or shared.
- **HbA1c**: A blood test showing average blood sugar over about three months; 6.5% or more is in the diabetes range.
- **HFR (Health Facility Registry)**: ABDM's registry of verified health facilities in India; a registered facility has a facility ID.
- **HMS / HIS**: Hospital management system or hospital information system: software that runs a hospital's operations and records.
- **HPR (Healthcare Professionals Registry)**: ABDM's registry of verified doctors, nurses and other health professionals.
- **IPD (in-patient department)**: Care for patients admitted to a hospital bed.
- **LIS**: Laboratory information system: software that manages lab orders, samples and results.
- **Medication adherence**: Taking medicines as prescribed: the right dose, at the right time, for the right duration.
- **MRN / UHID**: Medical record number or unique health ID: the number a hospital uses to identify one patient's record.
- **NABH**: National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers, part of the Quality Council of India, which accredits hospitals against quality standards.
- **OPD (out-patient department)**: Care for patients who visit and leave the same day, without admission.
- **PACS**: Picture archiving and communication system: stores and shows medical images.
- **PHR (personal health record)**: A health record kept and controlled by the patient.
- **PM-JAY**: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana: government health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospital care at empanelled hospitals.
- **Pre-authorisation**: Approval from an insurer, TPA or scheme before a planned treatment, so the hospital is paid.
- **QTc**: The QT interval of an ECG corrected for heart rate; prolongation raises the risk of dangerous arrhythmias.
- **RIS**: Radiology information system: manages radiology orders, scheduling and reports.
- **TPA (third-party administrator)**: A company that processes health insurance claims and cashless approvals for insurers.
- **Triage**: Sorting patients by how urgently they need care, usually in five levels in emergency departments.
- **WHO surgical safety checklist**: A checklist used before anaesthesia, before incision and before the patient leaves theatre, shown to reduce surgical complications.
